## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Two journal pages read on 2026-11-23 differ in emphasis. The editorial policy page says all manuscripts get single-blind review (author name revealed to referees, referees anonymous to authors) (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy). The submission guidelines page says the AEA has launched a three-year randomized controlled trial of author-anonymized ("double-blind") review and requires manuscripts to be anonymized (author names, affiliations, acknowledgement footnote, personal-website links and study-site identifiers removed, supplied in a separate title page) (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions). The AEA's announcement dated 2026-09-10 says the trial covers the AER, AER: Insights and the four American Economic Journals, expected to launch in fall 2026, and that identities are withheld from reviewers only in the treatment group (https://www.aeaweb.org/news/rct-announcement). How papers are assigned to the treatment group is not described on the pages read. Treat the review model as in transition and check the page before submitting |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Yes, inside the AEA family. After a rejection from the AER (or AER: Insights) the author can use a transfer option: the editorial office asks each referee for permission to share identity and cover letter, then forwards the decision letter and reports to the editor of the chosen American Economic Journal, who decides alone whether to reject, request a revision on the existing reports, or seek more reports. The page states that about 85% of transfers are rejected or summarily rejected at AEJ: Applied, 80% at AEJ: Micro and AEJ: Policy, and 75% at AEJ: Macro, with typical decision times of 1-3 months (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aej/faq-transfer-option, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No evidence on the pages read that reports are published; reports are forwarded to an AEJ editor only through the transfer option (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aej/faq-transfer-option) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Reviewers are asked to explain why the paper's execution and contribution do or do not suit the AER, and to separate essential from optional revisions (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/reviewers, retrieved 2026-11-23). A coeditor consults a second coeditor before giving a first revise-and-resubmit (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy). The editor and coeditors may return a manuscript without referee review, weighing the expected probability of meeting AER standards, breadth of topic and interest to the AER audience (same page) |

## Format

> Sources: https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions (submission), https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/accepted-article-guidelines and https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/style-guide (accepted-article stage), all read 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Regular articles; comments and replies (a comment must give a substantial, general-interest contribution beyond the original; no automatic right to reply) (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy). Crossref lists all 746 records in the window as journal-article type, so no other type is distinguishable there (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0002-8282,from-pub-date:2021-01-01) |
| **Word limit** | No word limit is stated. The page gives page-based advice: the average article runs 35-36 typeset pages, and manuscripts are strongly recommended not to exceed the length of 40 pages (11-point, 1.5 spacing, 1-inch margins) or 45 pages (12-point), including figures, tables, references and appendices (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | The limit is a strong recommendation, and the page says shorter, impactful papers also get full consideration (same page) |
| **Abstract limit** | 100 words or fewer, required (submission page); the style guide repeats the 100-word ceiling for articles, comments and replies (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/style-guide) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the page recommendation above. If bibliographic software is used, the page prefers Chicago Manual Author-Date style (submission page) |
| **Supplementary material** | In-paper appendices (proofs, derivations) are typeset and count toward length; an optional Supplemental Appendix is posted online unedited, and the paper must be self-contained without it (submission page). At acceptance, data and code go to an openly accessible trusted repository such as the AEA Data and Code Repository, with a README (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/accepted-article-guidelines) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit stated on the pages read (submission page, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Style / submission format** | PDF, under 10 MB where reasonably possible; the Style Guide is required for accepted articles and optional at submission; AEA templates may be used in "review mode"; submissions go through ScholarOne; a cover letter is not required, and a separate disclosure statement PDF from each author is required or the submission is incomplete and not reviewed (submission page). Field experiments must be registered in the AEA RCT registry (same page) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Contribution and fit with the AER audience are the stated screens: the editor and coeditors may return a manuscript without review, weighing expected probability of meeting AER standards, breadth of topic and interest to the AER audience (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy, retrieved 2026-11-23). Reviewers judge whether the paper's "execution and contribution to the literature" suit the journal (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/reviewers).
- **What kind of engagement?** The home page calls the AER a general-interest journal publishing on a broad range of topics, with 20 classification letters listed from A General Economics to Z Other Special Topics (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer). Papers must be self-contained: all essential data sources, definitions, methods and proofs belong in the paper, not in the Supplemental Appendix (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions).
- **Article type and length**: articles of about 35-36 typeset pages on average, with 40 pages (11-point, 1.5 spacing) strongly recommended as a ceiling and a 100-word abstract (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: no call for papers appears on the pages read; the AEA announced a trial of anonymized reviewing on 2026-09-10 (https://www.aeaweb.org/news/rct-announcement).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: papers previously rejected by the AER should not be resubmitted and will not be reviewed; a paper may be rejected without review (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions). Papers lacking per-author disclosure statements are treated as incomplete and not reviewed (same page).

| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. Qualitative wording is rare in abstracts (7 of 661, 1.1%, Crossref), which shows what the journal publishes, not how reviewers treat it | |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | Conflict rules: coeditors are recused for colleagues, graduate students, recent coauthors and advised untenured students; papers by a coeditor or the editor go to a guest editor (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy). Author side: 506 of 680 works have at least one US-based author (OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23) | https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Disclosure statements must say whether IRB approval was obtained for the project and, if not, why (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy, retrieved 2026-11-23). For anonymization, descriptions of IRB approvals that reveal the institution are omitted from the manuscript (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records: 130 of 670 Crossref records with author lists (19.4%), 2021-2026 (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No rule on independent scholars on the pages read. Authors give names and affiliations in a separate title page PDF (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23). Fees are higher for non-members of the AEA ($300 against $200 in high-income countries), so membership affects cost (same page) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Strict. Authors of papers with empirical work, simulations or experimental work must provide data, code and computation details sufficient to permit replication before acceptance, in an openly accessible trusted repository; a data editor checks compliance after conditional acceptance; exceptions exist where data cannot be public, with documented source and preserved code (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/policies/data-code, retrieved 2026-11-23). All data must be legally acquired (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | The submission page requires removing author names, affiliations, acknowledgement footnote, personal-website links and study-site identifiers from the manuscript, with identities supplied on a separate title page (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23). The editorial policy page still describes single-blind review (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/editorial-policy), and the announcement of the author-anonymized review trial (dated 10 September 2026) asks reviewers in the treatment group to refrain from seeking out author identities, says the design recognizes that reviewers may become aware of identities in other ways, and lists reviewer awareness of author identities as one of the outcomes to be measured (https://www.aeaweb.org/news/rct-announcement, read 2026-11-23). Anonymity is therefore not guaranteed |
| **AI use** | Disclose at submission; AI cannot be an author (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Submission fee $200 (AEA member, high-income country), $100 (middle-income), $0 (low-income); non-members $300, $200, $0; papers rejected without review get 50% back; accepted papers pay $15 per typeset page for papers first submitted on or after 2024-02-01 (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23). At the 35-36 page average that is about $525-$540 (arithmetic from the page's own figures) |
| **Originality screening** | All submissions are screened with Crossref Similarity Check (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Ethics and registration** | Field experiments must be registered in the AEA RCT registry, and the registration number is supplied at submission; laboratory experiments need not be registered "at this time" (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **No resubmission and no parallel submission**: papers previously rejected by the AER will not be reviewed, and papers under consideration at another journal are ineligible (Framing Requirements; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions).
- **Incomplete package**: submissions without a per-author disclosure statement are incomplete and not reviewed (Format; same page).
- **Data and code**: papers with empirical, simulation or experimental work must supply data and code sufficient for replication before acceptance, and field experiments must be registered in the AEA RCT registry (Practical Concerns, Format).
- **AI authorship**: AI software may not be listed as an author, and AI use must be described at submission (AI Policy).
- No hard blocker follows from a stated word limit: the journal states page-based recommendations only (Format).

### Soft Tax

- **Cost**: submission fee of $100-$300 by country income and membership, and $15 per typeset page on acceptance for papers first submitted on or after 2024-02-01 (Practical Concerns; https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aer/submissions).
- **Length**: an average article is 35-36 typeset pages and 40 pages is the recommended ceiling, appendices included (Format).
- **Replication effort**: a data-editor review after conditional acceptance (Peer Review; Practical Concerns).
- **Anonymization**: manuscripts must be anonymized and identities placed on a separate title page; prior work is cited in the third person (Voice & Style, Practical Concerns).
- **Time**: long. For articles published in 2025, submission to acceptance took 130 weeks, of which 38 were in the journal's own review process, plus 11 weeks from acceptance to publication (Review Cycle Time, 2026 Report of the Editor). First decisions: 77% within 3 months for 2025 submissions (projected).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical work in applied economics using randomized, quasi-experimental or structural designs and theory papers: 63, 47 and 149 of 661 abstracts (9.5%, 7.1%, 22.5%) (Methodological Preferences).
- Papers with a general-interest contribution across economics fields, given the journal's own description as general-interest and the screen on breadth of topic (Framing Requirements).
- Authors with replicable data: the journal's data and code requirement is strict (Practical Concerns).
- Co-authored work: 540 of 670 Crossref records with author lists have two or more authors (80.6%) (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Qualitative, interview-based, autoethnographic, mixed-methods or philosophical work: 7, 0, 0 and 0 of 661 abstracts respectively (Methodological Preferences). The counts show these are rare, not that they are rejected.
- Heterodox or institutionalist work: 0 of 661 abstracts with Marx, heterodox, post-Keynesian, institutionalist or evolutionary wording (Orientation), although the journal's classification list includes a heterodox-approaches class.
- Authors who cannot wait: about 39% of submissions in 2021-2025 were summarily rejected (usually within a week or two) and the report's maximum acceptance rate was 6.1% to 8.6% for submission years 2021-2024, against an 8 to 10 percent range the editor considers possible (Metrics, 2026 Report of the Editor); accepted papers took 130 weeks from submission to acceptance in 2025.

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> The AEA states that rejected AER papers can use a transfer option to an American Economic Journal, with 75-85% of transfers rejected at the AEJ stage (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aej/faq-transfer-option). The rows below name journals only; none has an entry in this corpus yet unless a link is shown.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | American Economic Journal (Applied Economics, Economic Policy, Macroeconomics or Microeconomics, chosen by field) | Transfer option forwards the AER reports to the AEJ editor; typical AEJ decision times 1-3 months (https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/aej/faq-transfer-option). Which AEJ suits depends on the paper |
| 2 | American Economic Review: Insights | The same transfer FAQ covers AER and AER: Insights as a pair; page length limits of Insights were not read |
| 3 | [Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization](journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization.md) | Behavioural and institutional economics neighbour with its own entry in this corpus (fit evidence is in that entry, not here) |
